spec_basis: STU-VID-033: '`flatten` bakes the current cut list into ordinary clips and discards the multicam mode; it is one reversible history step.'
STU-VID-040: 'Every operation in this sub-section is one reversible `StudioHistoryEntry` (14.19). ... A multicam record pass is one step.'
STU-VID-031: '`speed` is a rational multiplier ... Reverse is a negative speed.'
STU-VID-034: 'A CLIP marker travels with the clip and moves when the clip moves. A SEQUENCE marker is positioned in sequence time and does not move with clips.'
STU-VID-090 obligation 3: 'A determinate result is required for every refusal' (basis of the named refusals)
declared_readings: a records-only multicam step (switch without cut, toggles) advances the document revision by one with identical document content, so it is one history step with one receipt
a commit authority receives the successor document; the multicam records travel in the binding hash and the session stores the entry only when it publishes that successor

flatten at speed: piece media window = angle clip window cut to the overlap mapped through the angle-clip speed a; piece timeline span = overlap mapped through the multicam clip speed s; piece speed = exact reduced s*a; inexact -> multicam_speed_inexact
reverse speed on a multicam clip or an angle clip it reads -> multicam_reverse_unsupported (resolve and flatten)
resolve_active_angle floors a fractional source position (a slowed clip holds a source tick)

clip markers go to the piece holding their start (half-open spans), converted to media ticks; gap -> multicam_marker_in_gap, span past the piece end -> multicam_marker_spans_pieces, start outside the clip source window -> multicam_marker_outside_window; never converted to sequence markers
spec_deltas: STU-VID-033 states no flatten mapping for speed-changed multicam or angle clips (declared above)
STU-VID-033 states no flatten behaviour for reverse speed (declared refusal)
STU-VID-033 / STU-VID-034 state no flatten mapping for clip markers (declared above)
STU-VID-033 does not state how a multicam step that creates a source sequence is committed (declared: one session step with insert/remove inverse)
